ANGOSAT-2 provides satellite redundancy (GGPEN, May 2026); the INFOSI backup centre replicates it in real time since August 2026. Inaugurated at the end of April 2026, an $89m project occupying 6,225 m2, not stated whether building or campus (ITWeb, 15 June 2026). Inaugurated by the President on 28 April 2026 at Camama (Angop, PTI, 28 April 2026); Angop gives 208 racks and 1,040 kW at inauguration against the 336-rack design. The 12 modules were certified Tier III by Uptime in Presight's name, but the building had no Uptime certification as of June 2026, INFOSI awaiting an audit (Expansão, 1 June 2026); Angop's 1,040 kW is not stated as IT load.

The ministry's programme page (September 2026) describes it in the present tense as hosting state data, without a commissioning date. Allo Brazza (22 May 2026) still reported it 95% complete, with opening due in May 2026 and the national cloud in June; a September 2026 search found no report of its inauguration, so it stays Under construction. At an inspection on 22 September 2026 the vice-prime minister put works at 82% and said the centre would be operational by the end of 2026 or early 2027, with energy tests within a month; a 12 MW solar farm at Kintele is to back it because the digital minister said grid power alone would deter clients.

UNDP is supporting a national AI computing platform with NVIDIA GPUs at KoTDA (July 2026), and KoTDA signed an agreement with AWS on 18 August 2026 for an AWS Outpost at Konza; neither source says which facility will house them. KoTDA's ToR (March 2026): built from 2019, completed 2021. The KoTDA-AWS agreement (August 2026) provides for an AWS Outpost at Konza with no timeline or site named; not counted as a hyperscaler relationship until deployed.

September 2026 incident disrupted at least 12 government services; police engaged INTERPOL and will investigate after the consultant's report, with preliminary findings of corrupted files and no data stolen (2026-09-28).
